advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Include projectTypeKey (or a distinct label) in the attempts report so the two template-less fallbacks are distinguishable in the failure message.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:234-235: two bare candidates differ only by `projectTypeKey` (software vs. absent), which is not reflected in the attempt label
advisory.finding: The two template-less fallback candidates (software-typed and untyped) both report as `<no template>` in the aggregated failure message, so on total failure the report cannot distinguish which bare attempt failed with which status — weakening the diagnostic this change was written to improve.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm reusing the same project key across sequential create attempts cannot leave a partially-created project that makes later attempts fail with a misleading duplicate-key error.
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:239: `for payload in candidates:` — each payload shares the same `key` from `base`

ABSENCE: there is no teardown/DELETE of a possibly-created project between failed attempts, so a second attempt with the same key can be rejected for key collision rather than the underlying template problem
dropped.finding: All create candidates reuse the same project key across sequential POSTs with no cleanup between attempts; if any earlier attempt leaves the key registered (partial create, or a rejection that still reserved the key), later attempts fail with a duplicate-key error that masks the real cause in the final aggregated report.
